Lesson 9 · Business route

Audit the adjusted comparison

How much did a selected program help its eligible population?

Fictional case. The observations are generated for teaching, not evidence about a real business. The full data-generating process is in the technical appendix.

What the data show

The observed treated–control gap is 8.57 units. Regression standardization estimates an average effect of 3.86 units after using measured pre-program characteristics.

What would you decide?

State the target population, check that comparable treated and untreated units exist, and test whether unmeasured selection could change the recommendation.

Pause and explain

If adjusted groups look balanced, is the causal estimate proven?

Compare your reasoning

No. Balance covers measured variables. Hidden causes and weak overlap can still change the answer.

What the generator knows

Reveal the known truth after making your judgment

The generated average effect is 3.87. The script can reveal it because it created both potential outcomes; an actual program evaluation cannot observe that truth directly.

The truth belongs to this invented model. A real organization would still need to test the assumptions and collect its own evidence.
